title: A Landfall for the Current
premise: Paloma Almeida, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted in Chile and Argentina, is hired off the books to retrace a government survey team that vanished in the fjordlands of Patagonia, leaving intact gear, no tracks, and sealed orders no one will explain. With a runaway cartographer named Ines Vidal whose brother was on the team, Paloma discovers the survey was a cover for mapping a disputed mineral seam, and the 'vanishing' was a staged disappearance to bury the evidence and the men who refused to falsify it. As the monsoon floods the fjords and their boat begins to fail, Paloma must choose between selling his silence for reinstatement and exposing a minister whose career rests on the lie. He chooses truth, surviving the storm to deliver the team's hidden logbook, though the price is the last shred of his official reputation — and Ines, who came for her brother, learns he chose the lie and must decide whether love or loyalty survives it.
about_author: Beatrix Nystrom is a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent a decade outfitting survey teams across the southern fjords before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted boathouse on the coast of Norway, where the weather does most of her editing.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Working a low-grade ferry route in Puerto Natales, Paloma is offered an off-book contract by a fixer named Roldán: find out what happened to the survey vessel Cautiva. He refuses, then sees his blacklisting notice renewed in the harbor office. The beat is wounded pride curdling into necessity — he takes the job.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He reaches the Cautiva's last anchorage and finds tents pitched, rations stacked, radios charged — a camp abandoned mid-life, no tracks leaving it. The emotional beat is professional unease: everything about the scene is wrong in ways only a guide would notice, and the wrongness hooks him.

chapters.title: The Stowaway Logic
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines Vidal confronts Paloma at the anchorage, having tracked the same coordinates after her brother Tomás's letters stopped. She has a survey credential and a boat with a cracked hull. The beat is two suspicious strangers recognizing they need each other and hating it.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They negotiate an uneasy partnership: she has the government charts he can't legally touch; he has the fieldcraft to keep her alive. Paloma finds a sealed survey case hidden under the Cautiva's ballast, stamped with a ministry seal. The beat is transactional trust, sealed by a shared secret neither understands yet.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season Opens
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The first true storm hits as they enter the inner channels. Ines narrates the terror of a leaking hull and Paloma's unnerving competence. The beat is fear transmuting into grudging awe — she begins to see why the wilderness trusts him more than any government does.

chapters.title: What the Logbook Says
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They open the sealed case: survey readings for a massive lithium seam under disputed territory, with Tomás's annotations flagging the coordinates as falsified upstream. Paloma realizes the team didn't vanish — they were disappeared. The beat is the cold drop of understanding that the job is now a liability.

chapters.title: The Patrol Boat
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A naval patrol hails them; the officer, Lieutenant Ferrer, asks questions that are really warnings. Ines lies smoothly and realizes she's better at this than she should be. The beat is the first taste of how far the state's reach extends into empty water — and her own capacity for deception.

chapters.title: Roldán's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Via radio, Roldán reveals the contract's real client and offers Paloma a clean record in exchange for the case and silence about the seam. Paloma stalls. The beat is temptation laid out in the exact currency of his disgrace — legitimacy — and the shame of how long he considers it.

chapters.title: Tomás's Cache
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following her brother's annotations, they find his emergency cache in a sea cave: a duplicate logbook and a note naming the minister who ordered the falsification. Ines reads her brother's handwriting and understands he knew he might die. The beat is grief arriving before the facts do.

chapters.title: The Hull Gives
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The boat's cracked hull fails in open water; they beach on an uninhabited island with the monsoon peaking. Salvaging the case and the duplicate log becomes a desperate wet scramble. The beat is survival stripped to essentials — and Paloma realizing he's protecting the evidence like it's already his cause.

chapters.title: Island of the Living
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Stranded, they shelter, dry out, and finally talk honestly — her brother, his blacklistings, the mistakes that made them both exiles. Ines admits she suspects Tomás cooperated with the falsification before recanting. The beat is intimacy built from shared ruin, and the first unguarded trust between them.

chapters.title: Ferrer Returns
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The patrol boat finds them stranded; Ferrer offers rescue in exchange for the case, claiming the minister wants the team 'found alive' — a story already being written. Paloma reads the trap instantly. The beat is the corrupt bargain made polite, and Paloma's refusal costing them their rescue.

chapters.title: The Long Paddle
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. They repair the hull with salvaged canvas and resin and begin a slow, punishing run down the channels ahead of the storm front. Ines's arms fail; Paloma's don't. The beat is endurance as character — she learns the wilderness forgives nothing, and neither does he, least of all himself.

chapters.title: Witness in the Trees
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. In a fishing hamlet off the charts, an old fisherman recognizes the Cautiva's crew — he saw them taken aboard a ministry vessel at night, alive. The vanishing had witnesses after all. The beat is hope with teeth: the truth exists outside the logbooks, but so does the danger.

chapters.title: Roldán's Last Word
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Roldán makes the final offer: reinstatement, both blacklists lifted, Tomás's record quietly cleaned — if Paloma surrenders the case and lets the official story stand. Paloma asks what happened to the men. Roldán's silence answers. The beat is the moment loyalty to the wilderness of truth outweighs loyalty to his own redemption.

chapters.title: The Storm That Names Itself
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The season's worst system closes in as they make for the mainland press office in Punta Arenas. The hull fails again mid-crossing. Ines narrates the storm as a verdict: everything they've carried — grief, evidence, each other — tested at once. The beat is terror fused with resolve.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The climax: they drive the sinking boat onto a shingle beach in the storm's eye, the case lashed to Ines's back, Paloma's shoulder dislocated in the surf. Ferrer's patrol waits on the road beyond. Paloma chooses the open hills over the easy road. The beat is the cost of the choice made physical.

chapters.title: The Minister's Version
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Evading the patrol through the coastal forest, they hear Ferrer's loudhailer offering amnesty for the case and prison for its holders. Ines realizes the official story has already named her brother a deserter. The beat is fury as fuel — she stops running to survive and starts running to testify.

chapters.title: Press and Pressure
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They reach Punta Arenas and a journalist Roldán once warned Paloma about. The logbook, the cache, the fisherman's testimony assemble into a story the ministry can't smother. The beat is fragile triumph — truth published, but both of them now permanently marked.

chapters.title: What Tomás Chose
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The rescued crew surfaces, including Tomás, who admits he signed the falsified readings before recanting too late to save the others from detention. Ines confronts him: he chose his career, then his conscience, and it nearly destroyed everyone. The beat is love and betrayal forced into the same room.

chapters.title: Hearings and High Water
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The inquiry vindicates the crew and implicates the minister, who resigns into quiet exile; Roldán vanishes as fixers do. Paloma testifies, and his blacklists are lifted — but the agencies that once employed him now see him as a man who burns his employers. The beat is victory that doesn't restore what was lost.

chapters.title: A Landfall for the Current
chapters.summary: Paloma and Ines's alternating POV. Spring comes to the fjords. Paloma turns down the reinstated government contracts and takes Ines and Tomás's crew on as an independent survey partnership, answerable to no ministry. The final beat is quiet: the wilderness forgave nothing and forgot nothing, and neither did they — and that, at last, feels like home.
